mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about convex and concave lenses?

options.A: A convex lens is thicker at the centre than at the edges, while a concave lens is thinner at the centre than at the edges.
options.B: A convex lens always forms a real and inverted image of a distant object, whereas a concave lens always forms a virtual and upright image.
options.C: A concave lens can form a real and inverted image of a distant object.
options.D: The focal length of a convex lens is positive, while that of a concave lens is negative.

mcqs.answer: A concave lens can form a real and inverted image of a distant object.
mcqs.explanation: Convex lenses converge light and can produce real, inverted images of distant objects. Concave lenses diverge light, so they always produce virtual, upright images; they never form real, inverted images. Therefore option C is the false statement. The other options correctly describe the shape, image nature, and sign convention of focal lengths for the two lenses.

mcqs.question: A thin convex lens is struck by a ray that passes exactly through its optical centre. What happens to the ray after it emerges from the lens?

options.A: It bends towards the principal axis.
options.B: It bends away from the principal axis.
options.C: It continues in the same straight line without any deviation.
options.D: It gets reflected back towards the object.

mcqs.answer: It continues in the same straight line without any deviation.
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point where the principal axis meets the lens. At this point the thickness of the lens is negligible, so a ray passing through the optical centre experiences no net refraction and emerges undeviated. Options A and B describe refraction that occurs when the ray strikes the lens away from the centre, and D is unrelated to lens behaviour.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the principal focus of a convex lens with that of a concave lens?

options.A: The principal focus of a convex lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the object, whereas that of a concave lens is real and lies on the opposite side.
options.B: Both convex and concave lenses have real principal focuses located on the side opposite to the incident light.
options.C: The principal focus of a convex lens is real and lies on the side opposite to the incident light, while that of a concave lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the incident light.
options.D: The principal focus of a convex lens coincides with its optical centre, whereas for a concave lens it coincides with its vertex.

mcqs.answer: The principal focus of a convex lens is real and lies on the side opposite to the incident light, while that of a concave lens is virtual and lies on the same side as the incident light.
mcqs.explanation: For a converging (convex) lens, parallel rays meet at a real focus on the opposite side of the lens from the incoming light. For a diverging (concave) lens, the refracted rays appear to diverge from a virtual focus that is on the same side as the incoming light. Options A, B, and D misstate the nature or location of the focal points.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of a candle placed 30 cm from the lens on a screen 60 cm away on the other side. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula (Cartesian sign convention): 1/f = 1/v – 1/u, where u = –30 cm (object distance, negative) and v = +60 cm (image distance, positive). Thus 1/f = 1/60 – (‑1/30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20, giving f = 20 cm. The positive sign confirms a converging (convex) lens. Options A, B, and D result from incorrect arithmetic or misuse of sign conventions.
